Hook
hook
n. (a bent piece of metal for hanging or catching; rendering Hebrew vav, chach, chakkah)
From Anglo-Saxon hoc. The Hebrew name of the tabernacle hook, vav, became the sixth letter of the alphabet — a letter shaped like the peg it is named for.

Biblical Definition

Hook is a small word with two very different offices. In the tabernacle it is a fastening: the vail hangs “upon four pillars of shittim wood overlaid with gold: their hooks shall be of gold” (Exo 26:32), and the court's pillars are “filleted with silver; their hooks shall be of silver” (Exo 27:17). The metals are graded by nearness to the holy place — gold within, silver in the court, brass at the sockets — and the hooks are what hold the whole hanging structure together. That the Hebrew word vav is also the letter and, the conjunction that joins, is a happy providence of language. The second office is capture: the LORD tells Sennacherib, “I will put my hook in thy nose, and my bridle in thy lips, and I will turn thee back” (2Ki 19:28) — an empire led home like an animal. Amos threatens the same for the luxurious women of Samaria (Amo 4:2). What fastens the sanctuary also fastens the tyrant.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a hook as a piece of iron or other metal bent into a curve for catching, holding and sustaining any thing — and notes the pruning-hook and the fishing-hook as distinct kinds.

expand to see more

HOOK, n. A piece of iron or other metal bent into a curve for catching, holding and sustaining any thing; as a hook for hanging a pot.

2. A snare; a trap.

3. A curving instrument for cutting grass or grain; a sickle.

By hook and by crook, one way or other; by any means, direct or indirect.

Key Scripture

Exo 26:32 — "And thou shalt hang it upon four pillars of shittim wood overlaid with gold: their hooks shall be of gold, upon the four sockets of silver."

Exo 27:17 — "All the pillars round about the court shall be filleted with silver; their hooks shall be of silver, and their sockets of brass."

2Ki 19:28 — "Because thy rage against me and thy tumult is come up into mine ears, therefore I will put my hook in thy nose, and my bridle in thy lips, and I will turn thee back by the way by which thou camest."

Exo 38:10 — "Their pillars were twenty, and their brasen sockets twenty; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets were of silver."

Modern Corruption

Small and unglamorous offices despised in the body of Christ — the fastenings nobody names — while the age also forgets that God rules tyrants by a hook they never see.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is Paul's doctrine of the members, illustrated here in metal. No one ever admired a tabernacle hook. It is invisible when the work is done, and the whole vail hangs from it. A congregation that honours only its visible offices has misread the tabernacle inventory, in which the Holy Ghost troubled to record the metal of every hook and fillet. God's accounting includes the fastenings.

The second recovery is political and deeply comforting. Sennacherib came against Jerusalem in overwhelming force, and the LORD's answer was not an army but an image: I will put my hook in thy nose. The empire imagined it was choosing its route; it was being led. That is the doctrine of providence over rulers in its most vivid form, and it is the reason a believer may read the news without terror. The hooks that hold the sanctuary together and the hook in the tyrant's nose are held in the same hand.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew vav (H2053), a peg or hook — also the sixth letter of the alphabet; chach (H2397), a ring or hook put in the nose; chakkah (H2443), a fish-hook.

expand to see more

Hebrew vav (H2053) — a hook, peg; used only of the tabernacle fastenings, and the name of the letter that means and (Exo 26:32).

Hebrew chach (H2397) — a ring, hook, clasp; the hook in Sennacherib's nose (2Ki 19:28) and in leviathan's jaw (Job 41:2).

Hebrew chakkah (H2443) — a fish-hook; Habakkuk's image of nations taken up with the angle (Hab 1:15).

Usage

"“Their hooks shall be of gold” — the metal graded by nearness to the holy place."

"“Their hooks shall be of silver, and their sockets of brass” — God records the fastenings."

"“I will put my hook in thy nose” — an empire led home like an animal."
